p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio → p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio upward Heterogeneous per-agent contact ratios under quarantine aggregate into the layer-level ratio: agents who reduce contacts more strongly lower the quarantined mean degree, increasing suppression.

p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta → p6_meso_quarantined_degree_dispersion upward Heterogeneous individual reductions in degree under quarantine create a wider spread of contact degree among quarantined agents.

p6_meso_quarantined_degree_dispersion → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag downward High dispersion of contact degree among quarantined agents implies a heavy lower tail of very low-contact behaviour; an individual quarantined agent is then more likely to fall into the fully suppressed zero-contact category.

p6_meso_quarantined_degree_dispersion → p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio intra_scale Heterogeneous contact behavior among quarantined agents plausibly weakens layer-level suppression because some retain many contacts.

p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio downward Stronger layer-level degree suppression under quarantine means quarantined agents in that layer have relatively fewer contacts, mechanically lowering their individual quarantined-to-non-quarantined contact ratio.

p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio → p6_micro_quarantine_degree_delta downward Stronger layer-level suppression makes the quarantined-minus-non-quarantined degree difference more negative for agents in that layer, because quarantined agents reduce contacts more strongly.

p6_meso_layer_quarantine_suppression_ratio → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag downward A higher suppression ratio indicates quarantined agents in the layer achieve lower contact degrees, increasing the chance that an individual quarantined agent records zero contacts.

p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio downward Population contact-volume shifts change the baseline contact environment against which a quarantined agent’s contact reduction is measured.

p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag downward A large population contact decline can make it more likely that a quarantined individual records no contact edges at a step.

p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p6_macro_adherence_share intra_scale Population-wide contact volume changes can reflect and reinforce the share of quarantined agents whose degree remains below the non-quarantined median.

p6_macro_contact_volume_change → p6_macro_population_suppression_ratio intra_scale A drop in total contact volume is mechanically linked to stronger suppression of quarantined versus non-quarantined contact degree.

p6_macro_adherence_share → p6_micro_zero_contact_quarantined_flag downward A larger population share of quarantined agents contacting at or below the non-quarantined median can reinforce adherence norms, increasing the probability that an individual quarantined agent records zero contacts at a step.

p6_macro_adherence_share → p6_macro_population_suppression_ratio intra_scale Greater adherence among quarantined agents lowers their contact degree relative to others, increasing the population suppression ratio.

p6_macro_population_suppression_ratio → p6_micro_quarantine_contact_ratio downward A lower population-level quarantine suppression ratio indicates stronger overall activity reduction among quarantined agents, shaping the adherence context in which an individual quarantined agent’s own in-quarantine contact ratio is realised.
p6_macro_population_suppression_ratio → p6_macro_contact_volume_change intra_scale Stronger degree suppression among quarantined agents plausibly reduces population-wide contact volume change.
